KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a world-class durable franchise with dominant market share (45-46% global sparkling), asset-light concentrate model yielding ~29-30% operating margins, and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases. Q1 2026 results (reported 2026-04-28) showed strong momentum: 12% YoY revenue growth, 13% EPS beat vs consensus, 63% gross margin expansion, and management raised full-year EPS guidance to 8-9%. However, the stock is priced for this quality at ~27.7x trailing P/E (near the top of its 1-year range of 23.2-28.9x) and ~26x forward P/E, with an earnings yield of 3.6% below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.41%. WTI crude at $98.38 (+52.5% over the lookback) represents a material input-cost headwind. The $14B IRS tax dispute is a genuine tail risk. The consensus analyst target of $90 implies ~15% upside, but the stock has already re-rated to near-peak multiples without a clear earnings acceleration beyond high-single-digit growth. On balance, excellent franchise quality and recent operating momentum are offset by stretched valuation and macro headwinds, yielding a mildly positive but not compelling score.
